ISTJ.want: Finishing what you said you'd do, and being trusted
ISTJ.effort: Following the rules and steps without mistakes
ISTJ.work: Work with clear rules and steps, where getting it right matters

ISFJ.want: Being useful to people, and a place where you feel safe
ISFJ.effort: Noticing what's needed first and quietly helping
ISFJ.work: Work where you help people close by and hear "thank you" in person

INFJ.want: Doing things that feel meaningful, and people who really get you
INFJ.effort: Picking up on feelings people don't say out loud
INFJ.work: Work where you stay with people's worries and growth for a long time

INTJ.want: Moving things forward with your own plan, and time alone to think
INTJ.effort: Thinking ahead and finding the quickest way
INTJ.work: Work where you're trusted with long-term plans and systems

ISTP.want: Freedom to fix problems your own way, and time no one interrupts
ISTP.effort: Staying calm when something breaks and fixing it fast
ISTP.work: Hands-on work where you can see the results

ISFP.want: Being true to what you like, and calm relationships
ISFP.effort: Keeping the mood soft without making waves
ISFP.work: Work where you can use your taste and go at your own pace

INFP.want: Not having to give up what matters to you, and goals you truly like
INFP.effort: Trying to understand how people feel, and putting feelings into words or things
INFP.work: Work where you can express what you care about

INTP.want: Freedom to think things all the way through, and fun problems to chew on
INTP.effort: Figuring out how things work and spotting what doesn't add up
INTP.work: A place where thinking is the job

ESTP.want: Getting results right away by moving, and on-the-spot challenges
ESTP.effort: Acting without hesitating and grabbing the chance in front of you
ESTP.work: Work where speed and action turn straight into results

ESFP.want: Having a good time with people, and enjoying right now
ESFP.effort: Lighting up the room and making everyone have fun
ESFP.work: Work where you meet people face to face and see them smile

ENFP.want: New things that excite you, and being connected to people
ENFP.effort: Coming up with ideas and getting people to start something new with you
ENFP.work: Work with lots of new projects and new people

ENTP.want: Freedom to try new ideas, and people you can really debate with
ENTP.effort: Questioning the usual way and finding another one
ENTP.work: Work with lots of change, where ideas win

ESTJ.want: Sorting things out and moving them forward, and a role with responsibility
ESTJ.effort: Setting up the steps, pulling people together and getting results
ESTJ.work: Work where you run a team and see results in numbers

ESFJ.want: A place where everyone gets along, and hearing "thank you"
ESFJ.effort: Bringing people together and keeping things friendly
ESFJ.work: Work with a team or local community where you can be the one who pulls people together

ENFJ.want: Helping people grow their good side, and relationships built on trust
ENFJ.effort: Cheering people on and bringing a team together
ENFJ.work: Work where you teach or lead people

ENTJ.want: Moving people and things toward a big goal, and being the one who decides
ENTJ.effort: Making the call and running the team efficiently
ENTJ.work: Work where you make the decisions and aim for big results

worry: Time with people is fun, but you're wiped out once you get home
You can't say no to invites, and your week fills up
People think you're always cheerful, so no one notices when you're tired
IE.work: Work where you listen to people, then take it home and put it together on your own. Counseling, editing, research.
IE.key: When you get home today, put your phone down for 30 minutes and just zone out. Even if you like seeing people, you rest best alone.
IE.both: You can be bright and easy around people, but your energy comes back when you're alone. After a week full of plans, you may be more tired than you think.

worry: You want to see people, but plans still feel like a chore
After a few days at home, you start to feel low for no reason
You turn down an invite, then wish you'd gone
EI.work: Work where you prepare on your own and then share it with people. Small-team work, or planning things and presenting them.
EI.key: This week, ask just one easygoing friend, "Want to grab a coffee?" Seeing one person for a short time is easier than a big group.
EI.both: These days you value time alone, but you're someone who gets energy from people. When you go days without seeing anyone, your energy slowly drops.

worry: You have lots of ideas, but they all stop halfway
After talking big, you suddenly worry, "Can I really do this?"
Things often turn out different from what you pictured, and you feel let down
SN.work: Work where you take an idea all the way to something real. Making products, improving a shop or service, making things by hand.
SN.key: Pick one idea and do only the part that takes 5 minutes today. Looking something up or asking someone is enough.
SN.both: You enjoy thinking up new things, but at heart you want to check, "Does this actually work?" That may be why talk that's only ideas makes you uneasy.

worry: You do everything right every day, but it feels kind of dull
Doing the same thing over and over slowly wears you out
When someone asks, "What do you want to do?", you don't know what to say
NS.work: Work with a set routine but room to try your own ideas. Planning roles close to the front line, teaching, or being asked to improve how things are done.
NS.key: Today, take a different way home, or stop by a shop you've never been in. One small "first" can change your mood a little.
NS.both: These days you get things done step by step. But you're someone who likes wondering, "What could happen next?" When every day is the same, it starts to feel dull.

worry: You agree to go along, then realize later you didn't really agree
You have something to say, but you keep quiet so the mood won't sour
You listen to everyone's problems and put your own last
TF.work: Work where you listen closely, then make the call when it's needed. Counseling or support work, HR, healthcare, teaching, or keeping a team together.
TF.key: Next time you share an opinion, try this order: "I get how you feel. And here's what I think." You can stay kind and still say your view.
TF.both: You tend to go along with people kindly. But in your head, you're often calmly asking, "Is that actually right?" That may be why you swallow what you think.

worry: You know the answer, but you still can't decide
After giving your opinion, you keep replaying it: "Was I too harsh?"
Sometimes you lose track of what you actually care about
FT.work: Work where you take numbers and logic and make them make sense to people. Planning, marketing, editing, or helping customers with their questions.
FT.key: Pick one thing you're stuck on and ask yourself two questions, one at a time: "Which way does my heart say?" and "Which way does logic say?" You'll see what's holding you up.
FT.both: These days you decide with logic, but you're someone who cares a lot about how people feel. When logic says one thing and your heart says another, it can take you a while to decide.

worry: You act relaxed, but plans that aren't set keep nagging at you
You put things off, then blame yourself for it
When someone says, "Do whatever you like," it tires you out
JP.work: Work where the big picture is set but you choose how to get there. Running projects, organizing on-site work, running events.
JP.key: Before bed tonight, decide just one thing you'll do tomorrow. You don't need to plan it all; one fixed thing makes you feel lighter.
JP.both: You can roll with changes pretty easily. But you're someone who feels safe when things are decided, so days with no clear plan slowly wear you down.

worry: Everything's going to plan, but it isn't much fun
Sudden changes annoy you, even when you understand why
"I need to get it together" has become your catchphrase
PJ.work: Work where some days follow the plan and some days you decide on the spot. Sales, planning, managing on site, customer service.
PJ.key: Block out one half-day this week with nothing planned. On that day, just do whatever you feel like.
PJ.both: These days you plan ahead and get things done properly. But you're someone who likes to go with the mood. When every day is packed, it starts to feel suffocating.

worry: You're doing fine, but it still feels like "not enough"
You worry what people will think, so you hold back from what you want to do
A small mistake stays on your mind for days
AT.work: Work where avoiding mistakes matters, and sometimes you make the final call. Quality or risk control, healthcare, or being a leader's right hand.
AT.key: Tonight, think back on three things you got done today. Small things count.
AT.both: These days you're careful and check things before you act. You're someone who can go with your own judgment, so it may be okay to trust yourself a little more.

worry: You look so steady that you can't tell anyone you're worried
After deciding, you go back over it again and again on your own
The more people lean on you, the harder it is to admit you're struggling
TA.work: Work where you lead and make decisions, and checking the details matters too. Team leader, specialist roles, running a project.
TA.key: Tell just one person you trust, "Honestly, I'm a little worried." Just saying it can make things a bit easier.
TA.both: People see you as someone who decides without hesitating. But you're careful by nature, so inside you're probably often asking, "Is this really okay?"

same.both: Your temperament and character are the same type. How you naturally are and how you act now are close, so people tend to find you easy to read. Because your way of doing things is so clear, some places will suit you very well and others won't at all.
worry: Places where your way doesn't work wear you out fast
You don't know how to talk with people who think completely differently
Things go fine elsewhere, but where you are now, you keep spinning your wheels
same.key: Think of one place or person that's tiring you out right now, and spend a little less time there this week. For you, changing your distance tends to work better than changing yourself.
same.work: If the way you work now feels right, that's fine. When you're unsure, pick whichever option tires you out less.

letter.E: Gets energy from being with people
letter.I: Gets energy back with time alone
letter.J: Likes to stick to a plan
